item.title: Nagoya Festival: The Three Heroes Parade Through the City — Guide
item.description: The Nagoya Festival, held over a weekend in mid-October, is the city’s biggest annual celebration, and its heart is the Three Heroes procession: costumed riders portraying Oda Nobunaga, Toyotomi Hideyoshi and Tokugawa Ieyasu — the three unifiers of Japan, all born in what is now Aichi — lead some 600 participants in samurai armour through the streets between Nagoya Station and Sakae. Around the parade swirl historic karakuri mechanical-puppet floats, flower cars, marching bands and neighbourhood dance troupes, and many of the city’s museums and gardens open free for the weekend.

item.title: Hyakumangoku Matsuri: Kanazawa's Grand Samurai Procession Festival — Guide
item.description: Hyakumangoku Matsuri is Kanazawa’s largest annual festival, held each June to commemorate the 1583 entry of Maeda Toshiie into Kanazawa Castle, the event that established the powerful Maeda clan’s rule over the Kaga domain, whose rice yield of over a million koku gave the festival its name. The festival’s centrepiece is an elaborate procession of participants dressed in samurai-era costume re-enacting Toshiie’s triumphant entry, accompanied by traditional taiko drumming and dance performances, and the celebrations conclude with a lantern-lit boat parade along the Asano River.

item.title: Aizu Autumn Festival: A Samurai Procession Through History — Guide
item.description: The Aizu Autumn Festival is one of Tohoku’s largest historical re-enactment events, held each September in Aizu-Wakamatsu. Its centrepiece is a spectacular samurai procession — hundreds of participants in authentic-style armour, including a portrayal of feudal lord Gamo Ujisato, march through the city streets toward Tsurugajo Castle, alongside performances honouring the tragic Byakkotai cadets. The three-day festival also features traditional music, dance and food stalls throughout the historic city centre.
